article_title: Measuring Wigner functions of quantum states of light in the undergraduate laboratory
citation: Juan Rafael Álvarez, Andrés Martínez Silva, Alejandra Valencia. (2023). Measuring Wigner functions of quantum states of light in the undergraduate laboratory. arXiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.17525
title: Quadratures, Wigner distribution functions, and filtered back-projection as a phase-space characterization framework
description: The article's conceptual framework characterizes optical signals in a phase space spanned by two conjugate variables, the quadratures X and Y, which act as generalized position and momentum of the field. The Wigner Distribution Function represents any signal in this phase space: "it can be used to represent any signal u(x) in the phase space spanned by two conjugate variables X and Y." Because only marginal projections pr(s, phi) are experimentally accessible, the WDF is recovered from them via a filtered back-projection (Radon inverse transform) algorithm with a regularized kernel. The article presents this framework pedagogically, with a gallery of quantum states (Fock, coherent, vacuum, thermal, squeezed) each illustrated through density matrices, marginal distributions, Wigner functions and phasor diagrams.
requirements: Measurements rely on discretization of amplitudes and phases, so the Radon kernel must be regularized or filtered with a cutoff value kc to avoid ill behaviors
constraints: The WDF is not necessarily a positive function, making it a joint quasiprobability distribution between conjugate variables
target_learners: undergraduate and early graduate physics students in introductory quantum optics
target_learning_goals: understanding quadratures, Radon transforms, and their pivotal role in reconstructing Wigner distribution functions in quantum optics
examples: Section III consolidates a gallery of five quantum states of light, each shown via density matrix, marginal distributions, Wigner function and phasor diagram in Fig. 2
